battle.name: 第一次義衣戰爭
battle.brief: 一八九五年九月義大利自厄立特里亞攻入提格雷，遠征軍直指阿杜瓦；翌年三月一日，曼涅里克二世集結十萬以上大軍，義軍四旅一萬七千七百人、五十六門砲在縱隊分散後全軍崩潰，退回海岸。歐洲雷管步槍在高原晨霧裡射程仍遠，卻敵不住密集縱隊的近身衝鋒與快速砲火。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰雙方是義大利王國與衣索比亞帝國，中文維基把這一場收在第一次義大利—衣索比亞戰爭的名目之下。義大利方面是自厄立特里亞殖民地派出的遠征軍，行政與軍事指揮合一，由殖民地總督兼遠征總司令歐雷斯特·巴拉鐵里中將坐鎮阿斯馬拉，攻勢方向、行軍縱隊與後方補給都出他一人之手；作戰序列在阿杜瓦分為阿利別爾通、阿里蒙迪、埃萊納、達博爾米達四個旅，另有以厄立特里亞與提格雷當地人組成、由義大利軍官率領的阿斯卡里殖民步兵，約一萬人，分散配屬各旅作搜索、警戒與攻佔岩山；砲兵為野戰砲與山砲共五十六門，分屬各旅，火力配比隨步兵縱隊前進；後方補給以馬薩瓦港為起點，經通往阿斯馬拉的鐵路與公路，再轉牛車、騾馬與雇來的搬運工，遠征初期的糧秣全靠這條線撐住。衣索比亞方面沒有常備軍，靠皇帝曼涅里克二世向各省諸侯（稱拉斯、涅古斯）下令徵召：核心是紹阿與提格雷兩省年年操練的骨幹，其餘由戈賈姆、哈爾哈爾等省貴族自募，武器是長矛、弓箭、獸皮盾與各式步槍混編，馬隊與象隊擔任偵察與追擊，砲隊只有少數受過歐式訓練的砲手操縱舊砲；皇帝自任戰場總指揮，參謀是瑞士人阿爾弗雷德·伊爾格。外交通上以俄羅斯為唯一歐洲盟友，開戰前英國在倫敦支持義大利的殖民主張，法國則在軍火商層面大量售槍給衣索比亞，戰後法國在亞的斯亞貝巴的影響力反過來壓過義大利。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Kingdom of Italy and the Ethiopian Empire, and the Chinese Wikipedia lists this conflict under the title of the First Italo-Ethiopian War. On the Italian side stood the expeditionary corps sent out from the colony of Eritrea, where administrative and military command were joined in a single man, General Oreste Baratieri, colonial governor and commander-in-chief, who sat at Asmara and decided the direction of the advance, the marching columns and the supply arrangements himself. The order of battle at Adwa was divided into four brigades, those of Albertone, Arimondi, Ellena and Dabormida, together with colonial infantry recruited in Eritrea and Tigray and led by Italian officers, the askari, some ten thousand men in all, distributed among the brigades for scouting, outpost work and the storming of the massalas. The artillery amounted to fifty-six field and mountain guns, allotted to the brigades and moving forward with the infantry columns. In the rear the supply line started at the port of Massawa, ran by railway and road to Asmara, and then passed to ox carts, mules and hired porters; in the opening phase the whole army lived off that line. On the Ethiopian side there was no standing army at all. Emperor Menelik II called up the provincial notables, who bore the titles of ras and negus, and each of them raised his own men. The core was the seasoned infantry of Shewa and Tigray, while contingents from Gojjam, Harar and other provinces were raised by their own lords; the men carried spears, bows, hide shields and rifles of every kind mixed together, cavalry and elephant trains served for reconnaissance and pursuit, and the guns were worked by a small number of gunners trained in the European manner. The emperor was his own commander-in-chief in the field, with the Swissman Alfred Ilg as staff officer. In foreign affairs Russia was Ethiopia's only European ally; in London Britain supported the Italian colonial claim before the war, while France supplied arms to Ethiopia through her merchants, and after the war French influence at Addis Ababa outweighed the Italian.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的是曼涅里克二世。他一八八九年三月二十六日以約翰尼斯四世之子的身份登基，五月二日即與義大利簽下《烏查萊條約》，此後一八九三年宣布拒絕條約，一八九四年二月十二日照會義大利、宣稱自五月二日起不再履行任何權利義務；一八九五年九月十七日在沃雷伊盧發布全國動員令，各省兵在數週內湧向提格雷，一八九六年一月六日皇帝親率大軍抵達默克萊與馬科涅諾公爵會合，下令解除對默克萊守軍的圍困並放其帶槍離開，隨後駐紮豪齊恩與根本德帕塔一帶高地方針對阿杜瓦，在三月一日一戰中指揮分割突擊，並在義軍崩潰之後主動收兵不追。皇帝之妻泰圖貝圖爾親率五千名士兵上前線，並在後方督率砲隊射擊，是這場戰役中少數直接指揮作戰的女性。拉斯·阿盧拉早在一八八七年沙阿提與多加利之役中就以包抄擊敗義軍，戰前再派斥候偵得義軍縱隊分開，是阿杜瓦能逐一殲滅各縱隊的關鍵情報；戈賈姆的特克萊·海馬諾、拉斯·孟格沙·約哈尼斯、韋萊·貝圖爾等諸侯各率本部來援。瑞士人阿爾弗雷德·伊爾格自一八九三年起在巴黎經營軍火，一八九三年十一月以黃金與象牙換得八萬支格拉式一八七四步槍、三十三門砲與五千發砲彈，並曾勸皇帝採用歐式射擊陣形。義大利方面，總司令巴拉鐵里認定衣軍缺乏訓練、不足為慮，決定以二萬人與五十門砲在阿杜瓦外圍築成弧形包圍圈誘敵入甕，兵敗後在阿斯馬拉受審、免於刑責但被迫退役；安巴阿拉吉陣亡的托塞利少校、默克萊守將加利亞諾少校、接掌軍權的安東尼奧·巴爾迪塞拉，以及在阿杜瓦戰敗後兩週內被迫辭職的首相弗朗切斯科·克里斯皮，都是這場戰爭的關鍵人物。巴黎的義大利使節彼得羅·安東內利早在一八八四年就以五萬支雷明登步槍與一千萬發子彈換走六百頭載著黃金、象牙與麝香的駱駝；法國軍火商萊昂·舍夫努售予衣索比亞一萬五千支法軍在馬達加斯加戰事後淘汰的快射步槍；俄國志願者亞歷山大·布拉托維奇以紅十字會名義到前線服務，他寫下的見聞成為當時歐洲少數對衣軍實力的第一手記錄。
peopleEn: Menelik II decided how the war would go. He had been proclaimed emperor on 26 March 1889 as the son of Yohannes IV, and by 2 May of that year had already signed the Treaty of Wuchale with Italy; in 1893 he repudiated the treaty, and on 12 February 1894 he notified Italy that from 2 May onward he would perform none of its rights or obligations. On 17 September 1895 he issued the general call to arms at Were Ilu, and the provincial levies poured into Tigray within weeks. On 6 January 1896 the emperor arrived in person before Mekelle, joined the Duke of Macagno, released the Italian garrison and let it leave with its weapons, and then took up a position on the heights around Hawzien and Gendepata to face Adwa, where on 1 March 1896 he directed the attacks that cut the Italian columns apart and then stopped the pursuit. The empress Taytu Betul led five thousand of her own people to the front and supervised the artillery from the rear, one of the few women in that war to direct troops in the field. Ras Alula had already beaten the Italians by envelopment at Saati and Dogali in 1887, and before Adwa his scouts brought word that the Italian columns had separated; that intelligence was what allowed the Ethiopian army to destroy them one by one. Tekle Haymanot of Gojjam, Ras Mengesha Yohannes and Welle Betul all brought their own contingents. The Swissman Alfred Ilg had been buying arms in Paris since 1893, and in November of that year exchanged gold and ivory for eighty thousand Gras model 1874 rifles, thirty-three guns and five thousand shells, and he pressed the emperor to use European firing drills. On the Italian side Baratieri, convinced that the Ethiopian army was untrained and not worth fearing, chose to build a ring of fifty guns and twenty thousand men around Adwa and wait for the emperor to walk into it; after the defeat he was tried by a military court at Asmara, acquitted of any offence but forced out of the army. Also decisive were Major Toselli, killed at Amba Alagi, Major Galliano, who commanded the Mekelle garrison, Antonio Baldissera, who took over the command, and Francesco Crispi, the prime minister, who was driven to resign within a fortnight of the defeat at Adwa. In Rome the Italian envoy Pietro Antonelli had already swapped fifty thousand Remington rifles and ten million cartridges for six hundred camels loaded with gold, ivory and civet; the French arms dealer Léon Chefneux sold Ethiopia fifteen thousand quick-firing rifles surplus to the French in Madagascar; the Russian volunteer Alexander Bulatovich reached the front with the Red Cross, and his account became one of the few first-hand European descriptions of the Ethiopian army.
kits: 卡面上這件法國雷管步槍的技術血脈，幾乎就是這場戰爭裡兩軍步槍的共同祖先。一八四〇年式的法軍雷管槍把底火用在雷管上，槍機不必沾火藥，槍械在潮濕、塵土、寒冷的高原上仍能擊發；後來的格拉步槍一八七四年式、義大利一八九一年式卡爾卡諾、法國一八八六年式勒貝爾，都沿著雷管這條路走。衣索比亞正是靠這條路補上與歐洲的差距：一八九三年十一月由瑞士人伊爾格在巴黎購得八萬支法國格拉式一八七四步槍，連同三十三門砲與五千發砲彈；另從法國軍火商萊昂·舍夫努手上買得一萬五千支法軍在馬達加斯加戰事後淘汰的快射步槍；一八九四年底前又自俄國運入三萬支別爾丹步槍，光是法屬索馬里蘭運來的子彈就有至少二十五萬發，另有義大利一八八四年送出的五萬支雷明登步槍。阿杜瓦開戰前，義軍四旅配五十六門砲，衣軍則有近五十門砲，其中不少是法軍霍奇基斯快射砲，射速高於義軍野戰砲；衣軍步槍總數約十萬支，其中約半數屬快射一類。真正拉開距離的不是槍而是砲：義軍把全部火砲與約一萬一千支步槍丟在阿杜瓦，成為衣軍的繳獲，衣軍的砲兵與槍械供應自此改觀。義軍一側的骨幹是義大利本國的卡爾卡諾一八九一年式雷管後膛步槍（七點六五公釐），另有舊式步槍與卡賓槍，砲兵以野戰砲與山砲為主，遠征初期靠馬薩瓦港的船運與阿斯馬拉的鐵路接上火藥線，遠離海岸後全靠牛車、騾馬與雇來的搬運工維持。衣軍一方除火槍外還大量配備長矛、矛頭、盾牌與弓箭，馬隊用於迂迴，象隊負責運載；缺的是攻城器材、技術兵種與源源不斷的砲彈。這件雷管步槍在整個體系裡的位置因此很清楚：它讓一批只受過數週射擊訓練、穿著便服的徵召兵也能在數百公尺外穩定射擊，把義軍賴以取勝的射擊與陣地優勢抵銷了大半；但它解決不了火砲、鐵路與補給，衣軍最後是靠砲火與人數贏的。
kitsEn: The technical bloodline of the French percussion rifle on the card is very nearly the common ancestor of the rifles both sides carried in this war. The French pattern of 1840 put the priming on the percussion cap, so that the weapon needed no loose powder about the pan and would still fire in damp, dusty and freezing conditions on the high plateau; the Gras model 1874, the Italian Carcano model 1891 and the French Lebel model 1886 all followed that same line. Ethiopia closed the gap with Europe precisely along it: in November 1893 the Swissman Ilg bought eighty thousand French Gras model 1874 rifles in Paris, together with thirty-three guns and five thousand shells; from the French arms dealer Léon Chefneux she bought another fifteen thousand quick-firing rifles surplus to the French forces after the Madagascar war; before the end of 1894 thirty thousand Berdan rifles arrived from Russia, at least a quarter of a million cartridges came in through French Somaliland, and Italy had handed over fifty thousand Remington rifles back in 1884. At Adwa the Italians had fifty-six guns to the Ethiopians' nearly fifty, many of the latter being French Hotchkiss quick-firing pieces that outpaced the Italian field guns; of the Ethiopian rifles, about a hundred thousand were in service and roughly half of them were quick-firing. What really separated the two sides was not the rifle but the artillery: the Italians abandoned every gun and some eleven thousand rifles at Adwa, and the capture transformed the Ethiopian war effort. The Italian backbone was the Carcano model 1891 percussion breech-loading rifle in 7.65 calibre, backed by older muskets and carbines, with field and mountain guns, and in the opening phase the ammunition line ran by sea from Massawa and by the railway to Asmara; once inland, everything moved on ox carts, mules and hired carriers. The Ethiopians matched their firearms with spears, javelins, shields and bows, used cavalry for turning movements and elephants for transport; what they lacked were siege equipment, technical trades and a steady flow of shells. The place of this percussion rifle in the whole system is therefore plain: it let levies trained for a few weeks and dressed in civilian clothes shoot steadily at several hundred metres, cancelling most of the Italian advantage in marksmanship and position; but it could not supply artillery, railways or logistics, and the Ethiopians won on guns and on numbers.
tactics: 義軍的戰術建立在兩個前提上：以正規軍的射擊與工兵技術壓制對方，以縱隊與迂迴把分散的敵軍各個吃掉。行軍以旅為縱隊，沿阿斯馬拉至阿迪格臘特公路北進，到阿杜瓦後在城北高地築起連續胸牆與塹壕，把五十六門砲架在射界內，形成一個向北敞開的弧形包圍圈，企圖把皇帝的主力引進來一次殲滅；一八九六年二月二十九日夜，三個旅分三路縱隊出營，企圖側擊包抄，第四旅留營。但高原夜路狹窄荊棘、彎多霧重，行軍中各旅彼此拉開數公里，到天明時已不成建制；命令與旗號在山谷裡傳不開，各旅不知道自己人在何處，砲兵雖攔住了頭一股進攻的衣軍，卻無法支援被分隔的步兵。到了三一日上午九時後局勢逆轉，衣軍在阿利別爾通縱隊、古索索山、瑪里安謝維托河谷三處同時發動，正面攻擊與側翼縱深同時展開，把三個意縱隊各個咬住；皇帝的參謀請他投入二萬五千人的預備隊，這支預備隊投入後雙方一度相持，中午之前戰局定下。衣軍的戰術要點有四：一是以師旅為單位多路合圍，不把兵力押在一點；二是分割敵縱隊後逐個殲滅，讓義軍無法互相支援；三是重視近身戰力，長矛、刺刀與馬刀在坡地與巖隙裡發揮作用；四是砲隊放在後方由觀察員指引射擊，射程與射速都勝過對方。圍城也是戰術的一部分：默克萊守軍約二百名義大利人與一千一百五十名阿斯卡里被切斷飲水後，在一八九六年一月二十一日投降；皇帝不但准許他們帶槍離開，還借出騾馬給他們撤回，卻藉此把自己的大軍調到豪齊恩與根本德帕塔的高地。衣軍攻占安巴阿拉吉等岩山後佔據制高點，把義軍壓在低地。最後一點同樣是戰術性的：皇帝在勝利後沒有追擊，也沒有向厄立特里亞進攻，把戰場停在可以談判的地方。
tacticsEn: Italian tactics rested on two assumptions: that regular-arm marksmanship and engineering would beat the enemy, and that columns and turning movements would destroy an enemy that had split up. The army marched by brigades in column along the road from Asmara to Adigrat, and once at Adwa it built a continuous breastwork and trench line on the heights north of the town, with fifty-six guns covering them, forming a ring open to the north in the hope of drawing the emperor's main body into it and destroying it in one stroke. On the night of 29 February 1896 three brigades broke camp in three columns to strike the flanks, with the fourth left in camp. But the highland tracks were narrow and thorny and the nights misty, the columns stretched over several kilometres, and by dawn they were no longer formed units; orders and signals could not pass in the valleys, the brigades did not know where the others were, and although the guns checked the first Ethiopian assault they could not support infantry that had been cut off. After about nine in the morning the tide turned, when the Ethiopians struck simultaneously in three places, at the column of Albertone, on Mount Gusoso and in the valley of Mariam Shewito, combining frontal assault with movement in depth and closing on each Italian column in turn. The emperor's staff urged him to commit a reserve of twenty-five thousand men; once that reserve entered, the battle was balanced for a time, and by noon it was decided. Four points stand out in the Ethiopian method. First, they converged in several divisions and brigades rather than staking everything on one point. Second, once the enemy columns were cut apart they were destroyed one by one, so that the Italians could never support one another. Third, they put weight on close combat, with spears, bayonets and sabres working in the slopes and the rock clefts. Fourth, the guns were placed in the rear and fired on the direction of observers, with both range and rate of fire better than the enemy's. Siege was part of the method as well: the Mekelle garrison, about two hundred Italians and eleven hundred and fifty askari, was cut off from its water and surrendered on 21 January 1896; the emperor allowed it to leave with its weapons and even lent it mules for the march back, and used the time to move his own army onto the heights at Hawzien and Gendepata. After taking the massalas at Amba Alagi and elsewhere they held the high ground and pressed the Italians down into the low ground. The last point was strategic as much as tactical: having won, the emperor neither pursued nor advanced into Eritrea, and left the field open for negotiation.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。時間線：一八八九年五月二日《烏查萊條約》簽訂；一八九三年曼涅里克宣布拒絕；一八九四年十二月義軍越過梅雷布河進入提格雷；一八九五年九月十七日皇帝發布動員令；一八九五年十二月七日安巴阿拉吉之役義軍第一次敗；十二月十八日圍困默克萊；一八九六年一月二十一日默克萊守軍投降；一八九六年三月一日阿杜瓦開戰；一八九六年十月二十六日《亞的斯亞貝巴條約》簽訂；一九〇〇年起沿梅雷布河劃界。兵力：義大利遠征計畫調度一萬四千人，阿杜瓦作戰時四旅合計約一萬七千七百人、五十六門砲；衣軍參戰人數各說七萬三千至十二萬不等，其中約十萬人持有步槍，火砲近五十門；安巴阿拉吉一役，托塞利少校以下大部分守軍陣亡，阿里蒙迪以四百人退回默克萊，默克萊守軍為二百名義大利人與約一千一百五十名阿斯卡里。損失：阿杜瓦一戰，義軍陣亡約五千九百至六千一百人（其中軍官約三百人），受傷約一千四百人，被俘的義大利人約一千八百人、阿斯卡里一至二千人；衣軍陣亡約三千九百至七千人，受傷約六千至一萬人；義軍丟下全部火砲與約一萬一千支步槍。軍火數量：《烏查萊條約》附贈三萬支步槍與二十八門砲；一八八四年五萬支雷明登與一千萬發子彈；一八九三年八萬支格拉式、三十三門砲與五千發砲彈；一萬五千支法軍淘汰快射步槍；一八九四年底前三萬支俄國別爾丹；法屬索馬里蘭運入至少二十五萬發子彈。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The chronology: the Treaty of Wuchale was signed on 2 May 1889; Menelik repudiated it in 1893; the Italians crossed the Mereb River into Tigray in December 1894; the emperor issued the call to arms on 17 September 1895; the Italians lost at Amba Alagi on 7 December 1895; Mekelle was invested on 18 December; the Mekelle garrison surrendered on 21 January 1896; Adwa was fought on 1 March 1896; the Treaty of Addis Ababa was signed on 26 October 1896; and the frontier was delimited from 1900. Strength: the Italian expedition was planned at fourteen thousand men, and the four brigades that fought at Adwa totalled about seventeen thousand seven hundred men with fifty-six guns; the Ethiopian force is given at between seventy-three thousand and one hundred and twenty thousand men, of whom about one hundred thousand carried rifles, with nearly fifty guns. At Amba Alagi Major Toselli and most of the garrison were killed, Arimondi fell back to Mekelle with four hundred men, and the Mekelle garrison consisted of two hundred Italians and about eleven hundred and fifty askari. Losses: at Adwa the Italians lost about five thousand nine hundred to six thousand one hundred dead, of whom some three hundred were officers, about one thousand four hundred wounded, and about eighteen hundred Italians and one to two thousand askari taken prisoner; the Ethiopian dead are given at about three thousand nine hundred to seven thousand with six thousand to ten thousand wounded; the Italians left behind every gun and some eleven thousand rifles. On the material side the Treaty of Wuchale had brought thirty thousand rifles and twenty-eight cannon; fifty thousand Remington rifles and ten million cartridges were supplied in 1884; eighty thousand Gras rifles, thirty-three guns and five thousand shells were bought in 1893; fifteen thousand surplus French quick-firing rifles followed; thirty thousand Russian Berdan rifles had arrived before the end of 1894; and at least a quarter of a million cartridges came in through French Somaliland.
cause: 起因是《烏查萊條約》第十七條的文字之差。義大利一八七〇年完成統一後急需殖民地，一八八五年在英國支持下取得馬薩瓦至貝盧爾一段海岸，卻在一八八七年沙阿提與多加利之役中被拉斯·阿盧拉包圍全滅，退回海岸；一八八九年約翰尼斯四世戰死，曼涅里克登基，五月二日與義大利簽約，義方以三萬支步槍與二十八門砲換取二百萬里拉，並把北部大片土地與紅海沿岸據為己有。義大利文的第十七條寫的是衣索比亞的對外事務須經由義大利進行，阿姆哈拉文寫的卻只是可以借道義大利使館辦事，兩種理解相差不可以道理計。義大利單方面宣布保護國，衣索比亞不予承認，衝突便由外交轉為邊界上的零星交火；一八九〇年合併成立的厄立特里亞殖民地也步步進逼。義方先試過別的辦法：以兩百萬發子彈的賄賂換取對第十七條的承認，被皇帝拒絕；又想策反提格雷王公曼加沙，許以金錢與武器推翻曼涅里克，同樣沒有成功。於是羅馬選擇用軍力解決，克里斯皮內閣相信技術與訓練足以抵銷數量上的差距，遠征軍在一八九四年底越過梅雷布河，一八九五年全面進攻提格雷。
causeEn: The cause lay in the wording of Article XVII of the Treaty of Wuchale. Having completed its unification in 1870, Italy needed colonies, and in 1885, with British backing, it took the coast from Massawa to Belul; but at Saati and Dogali in 1887 it was enveloped and destroyed by Ras Alula and driven back to the shore. Yohannes IV died in 1889, Menelik was proclaimed, and on 2 May the treaty was signed: Italy handed over thirty thousand rifles and twenty-eight cannon in return for two million lire and the northern territories with the Red Sea coast. The Italian text of Article XVII said that Ethiopia's foreign affairs were to be conducted through Italy; the Amharic text said only that she might use the Italian legation for that purpose, and the distance between the two readings was not a matter of interpretation. Italy declared a protectorate on its own authority, Ethiopia refused to recognise it, and the conflict moved from the diplomatic to the border in a series of skirmishes; the colony of Eritrea, merged in 1890, pressed forward step by step. Italy tried other methods first. An offer of two million cartridges in return for a recognition of Article XVII was refused by the emperor, and an attempt to win over the Tigrayan prince Mangasha, with money and weapons to overturn Menelik, failed as well. Rome then chose force, and the Crispi government believed that technical superiority and training would cancel the difference in numbers; the expedition crossed the Mereb River at the end of 1894 and advanced into Tigray in full in 1895.
impact: 影響有遠有近。對義大利，這是一場政治地震：阿杜瓦敗訊傳回國內，羅馬與各大城市爆發示威與暴動，首相克里斯皮在兩週之內被迫辭職，遠征總司令巴拉鐵里在阿斯馬拉受軍法審判，雖獲判無罪仍被免職退休，義大利的殖民聲望跌到谷底，海外冒險不再受到輿論支持。對衣索比亞，這是國運的轉折：曼涅里克不僅守住了疆土，還從義軍手裡繳獲全部火砲與一萬一千支步槍，軍備為之一變，國家的向心力也因一場共同的勝利而提高；德國相俾斯麥曾嘲諷義大利在非洲的冒險，說義大利人胃口極大，牙齒卻壞得厲害。國際層面：俄羅斯以紅十字會名義派出醫療隊，雖然抵達得太遲而未及參戰，卻加深了衣索比亞與俄國之間的同教之誼；戰後英國改弦更張，一八九七年五月十四日與衣索比亞簽約，承認其獨立並交換邊界，法國則於一八九七年三月二十日簽下帶有同盟性質的條約，取代義大利成為皇帝宮廷裡最有影響力的外來力量。長期看，這場戰爭成了非洲人抵抗殖民政權的象徵：一九三五年義大利再攻衣索比亞時這段記憶被一再援引，一九四一年英軍在東非戰役中接應衣軍游擊隊把義大利人逐出衣索比亞；疆界的劃分也延到一九〇〇至一九〇二年才沿梅雷布河完成，奠定了今日衣索比亞與厄立特里亞的疆界基礎。
impactEn: The effects reached far in both time and direction. In Italy the defeat was a political earthquake: the news from Adwa set off demonstrations and riots in Rome and in the other cities, the prime minister Crispi was forced to resign within a fortnight, and the commander-in-chief Baratieri was tried by court martial at Asmara, acquitted but compelled to retire; Italian colonial prestige fell to its lowest point and overseas adventure lost its hold on public opinion. For Ethiopia it was a turning point in the fortunes of the state: Menelik had not merely held his frontiers, he had taken every gun and some eleven thousand rifles from the Italians, which transformed the country's war effort, and the sense of common purpose rose with a victory shared by every province. The German chancellor Bismarck once mocked the Italian adventure in Africa, saying that the Italians always had enormous appetites but poor teeth. At the international level Russia sent a medical mission under the Red Cross which, though it arrived too late to take part in the fighting, deepened the bond of common faith between Russia and Ethiopia. After the war conservative opinion in London changed course: on 14 May 1897 Britain signed with Ethiopia, recognised her independence and exchanged frontiers, and on 20 March 1897 France concluded a treaty of a markedly alliance-like character, replacing Italy as the most influential foreign power at the imperial court. In the long run this war became a symbol of African resistance to colonial rule. When Italy invaded Ethiopia again in 1935 the memory of 1896 was invoked repeatedly, and in 1941 British forces in the East African campaign supported Ethiopian guerrillas in driving the Italians out. The colonial partition was completed only between 1900 and 1902 along the Mereb River, laying the basis for the present frontier between Ethiopia and Eritrea.
result: 結果是義大利認輸，衣索比亞完好。一八九六年三月一日阿杜瓦一戰，意軍四個縱隊在晨霧中被逐個切斷，砲與槍全數丟棄，數千殘兵退回合蘭；義軍沒有乘勢攻入厄立特里亞，兩個月的談判後，一八九六年十月二十六日簽下《亞的斯亞貝巴條約》：義大利承認衣索比亞的獨立毫無保留，廢除《烏查萊條約》，衣索比亞則承認義大利對厄立特里亞的統治並釋放全部義大利戰俘。一九〇〇年起雙方沿梅雷布河劃定邊界，這條線後來成為兩國的國界。義大利國內的清算隨之而來：克里斯皮內閣倒台，巴拉鐵里被解職退休，遠征軍退回馬薩瓦與阿斯馬拉之間的海岸地帶，厄立特里亞殖民地從此定型為一個僅有數千平方公里的沿海據點，直到一九三五年再被義大利擴充成更大的領地。對衣索比亞而言，這場戰爭的收穫遠不止一紙條約：皇帝以主動克制換來歐洲列強的承認，軍隊在阿杜瓦繳獲的歐式火砲與步槍讓衣軍的火力脫胎換骨，而非洲國家在決定性會戰中擊敗歐洲殖民軍這件事本身，成了此後數十年非洲各地民族主義的引信。
resultEn: The result was that Italy accepted defeat and Ethiopia came through intact. On 1 March 1896 the Italian columns were cut apart one after another in the morning mist at Adwa, guns and rifles were thrown away, and several thousand survivors fell back to Gheha; the Ethiopians did not follow them into Eritrea, and after two months of negotiation the Treaty of Addis Ababa was signed on 26 October 1896. Italy recognised the independence of Ethiopia absolutely and without reserve, annulled the Treaty of Wuchale, and Ethiopia in return recognised Italian rule over Eritrea and released all Italian prisoners. The frontier was drawn along the Mereb River from 1900, and that line later became the border between the two countries. The reckoning in Italy followed at once: the Crispi cabinet fell, Baratieri was dismissed and retired, and the expeditionary army withdrew to the coastal strip between Massawa and Asmara, leaving Eritrea as a small foothold of a few thousand square kilometres until 1935, when Italy enlarged it into a far greater territory. What Ethiopia gained went well beyond the treaty. By holding back, the emperor bought recognition from the European powers; the European guns and rifles captured at Adwa rebuilt the firepower of the Ethiopian army; and the fact that an African state had beaten a European colonial army in a decisive field engagement became in itself a fuse for the nationalism of the following decades.
